# wavpack / fuzzer

wavpack's own fuzz target `fuzzer` ([source](source/fuzzer.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over WavPack (dbry/WavPack at eccf998c).

Opens the input as a WavPack stream (tags, wrapper, DSD-as-PCM, OPEN_NO_CHECKSUM, 4 worker threads), calls ~25 getters, reads all tag items, appends tags, decodes all samples, reads the MD5 sum, seeks and writes tags back to a discarding writer. The MD5 sum is fetched but never compared with the decoded samples, and checksums are disabled by OPEN_NO_CHECKSUM.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against WavPack at commit eccf998c.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.

The harness turns some inputs away by returning a value other than 0 or -1, which the driver reports as status 78, so its halts statements allow 78 as well:
- An input WavpackOpenFileInputEx64 cannot open as a WavPack stream is returned 1 ([lines 148-153](source/fuzzer.cc#L148-L153)).

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch wavpack` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzzer.plain` | 119,848 | `e98d577e8cc0b150a4c4bcee0270a98a6b4e54b943a2c376b8f62d4add73b52e` |
| ubsan | `fuzzer.ubsan` | 136,200 | `edbfadaed4243c36aa6d055dfa57ecf7283d142ffe786d481fbf67e9c69b3ee8` |
| asan | `fuzzer.asan` | 937,272 | `c3bf89199ed1ac7449d43c401833ffc5c0b2dfedb2e3652462084daed49bc199` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzzer.asan-ubsan` | 956,504 | `6227fb7265c0de9da3ba85df850980c0d397d09c88b78eaf6a09240f2ffa9e26` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
